summary: @servicetitan/examples ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper executing 727KB obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = 'node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is itself hex-obfuscated: it probes for a local `bun` binary and, when absent, downloads the Bun runtime for the detected platform/arch from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against the sibling math_init.js. math_init.js is a single-line ~727KB JS blob with a shuffled string array, an index rotator (WV8StW), a giant numeric decoding table (n7gIxM), and a custom base-alphabet decoder (hc1jfK9) — opaque to static review. The package advertises itself as a ServiceTitan React UI examples package, and its src/ tree contains benign-looking.tsx examples plus many @servicetitan/* dependencies pinned around 16.0.0; the setup.mjs + math_init.js dropper is unrelated to that declared purpose. Fetching a second-language runtime at install time to execute an obfuscated sibling payload is an alternate-runtime dropper pattern that evades Node-based scanners, and the scope match to ServiceTitan's real component libraries is consistent with scope impersonation aimed at ServiceTitan build environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
